most_likely_actual_diagnosis_free_text: Mild acute pancreatitis caused by a mass in the pancreatic body. The most likely causes are pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with upstream duct obstruction or focal (mass-forming) autoimmune pancreatitis; primary pancreatic lymphoma is less likely.
one_line_reason: The patient has epigastric pain and a lipase more than 3 times the upper limit of normal, which meets the criteria for acute pancreatitis. The underlying cause is a 4 x 2 cm pancreatic body mass with restricted diffusion and mild dilation of the duct beyond it, with no alcohol or drug cause. That mass is a lesion outside the listed diagnoses, so the listed acute pancreatitis leaf describes the syndrome, not the cause.
